title: General interview questions — Module Quiz
description: Mixed quiz covering all topics in General interview questions.

questions.question:
What is the output?
console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3);
questions.explanation: Floating-point rounding makes 0.1+0.2 ≈ 0.30000000000000004, so the strict equality is false.

questions.question: Explain `==` vs `===` in one rule.

options.text: == allows type coercion, === compares value AND type (strict)

questions.explanation: == coerces types before comparing; === is strict (no coercion). Prefer ===.

questions.question: What is a closure?

options.text: A way to close the browser tab
A function that remembers variables from its lexical scope even after the outer function returns

questions.explanation: Closures capture the enclosing scope, enabling data privacy and factory functions.

questions.question: What does `this` refer to inside a regular (non-arrow) method called as `obj.method()`?

options.text: obj (the object the method was called on)

questions.explanation: For normal functions, `this` is the receiver of the call (obj in obj.method()).

questions.question: What is the difference between `let`, `const`, and `var`?

options.text: var is function-scoped & hoisted; let/const are block-scoped; const cannot be reassigned
const is block-scoped, others are global

questions.explanation: var hoists to function scope; let/const are block-scoped (TDZ); const binding is immutable.

questions.question: What is the Temporal Dead Zone?

options.text: The span between entering a scope and a let/const declaration, where access throws ReferenceError
A type of error in Promises

questions.explanation: TDZ: let/const are hoisted but uninitialized; referencing them before declaration throws.

questions.question: How do you deep clone an object in modern JS?

options.text: structuredClone(obj), or for simple cases JSON round-trip (but loses functions/Dates)

questions.explanation: structuredClone handles nested objects; JSON round-trip fails on functions, Date, undefined, Map/Set.

questions.question: What is `event delegation`?

options.text: Attaching one listener to a parent to handle events from many children via bubbling

questions.explanation: Delegation leverages event bubbling so a single parent handler manages dynamic child elements efficiently.

questions.question: What will `typeof null` return?
questions.explanation: typeof null returns 'object' due to a legacy JS implementation quirk.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `debounce` and `throttle`?

options.text: To limit how often a function runs on rapid events (debounce = after idle; throttle = at most once per interval)

questions.explanation: Debounce delays until activity stops; throttle caps execution frequency. Both improve performance on scroll/resize/input.

questions.question: What is the difference between NgModule-based and Standalone components?

options.text: Standalone components declare their own imports and need no NgModule declaration

questions.explanation: Standalone (v15+) components import their dependencies directly; bootstrapping can skip NgModules.

questions.question: What is the role of `HttpClient` and `HttpInterceptor`?

options.text: HttpClient performs HTTP calls; interceptors transform requests/responses (auth, logging, errors)

questions.explanation: Interceptors sit in the request pipeline — ideal for adding tokens, retrying, or standardizing error handling.

questions.question: What is the difference between template-driven and reactive forms?

options.text: Template-driven = directives in HTML (simple); reactive = explicit FormGroup/FormControl in TS (testable, scalable)

questions.explanation: Reactive forms give immutable, observable, unit-testable state; template-driven is quicker for trivial forms.

questions.question: What are generics and why use them?

options.text: Type parameters that let functions/types work over many types while preserving type safety

questions.explanation: Generics (e.g. identity<T>) enable reusable, type-preserving abstractions like Array<T> and Promise<T>.

questions.question: What is a `union type`?

options.text: A type that can be one of several types, e.g. string | number

questions.explanation: Unions express 'this OR that' and are narrowed with typeof/discriminated unions.

questions.question: What is the difference between `rem` and `em`?

options.text: rem is relative to the root font-size; em is relative to the parent/element font-size

questions.explanation: rem = root element size (predictable); em = cascades with parent size (can compound).

questions.question: How do you center a div horizontally AND vertically (modern approach)?

options.text: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; (on the parent)

questions.explanation: Flexbox (or grid place-items: center) is the standard cross-browser centering technique.

questions.question: What does `box-sizing: border-box` do?

options.text: Includes padding & border inside the element's declared width/height

questions.explanation: border-box makes width include padding+border, making layouts predictable (common reset).

questions.question: Interviewer: 'Tell me about a time you improved performance in a frontend app.' Best structure?

options.text: STAR: Situation, Task, Action, Result — with a metric (e.g. load time -40%)

questions.explanation: Behavioral answers win with concrete context, your specific action, and a measurable outcome.

questions.question: When asked 'What is your biggest weakness?', a strong answer...?

options.text: Names a real, non-fatal area and what you're doing to improve it

questions.explanation: Self-awareness + growth mindset beats canned 'perfectionist' answers.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the purpose of "General interview questions"?

options.text: It is a focused area of frontend knowledge with its own set of patterns and trade-offs.
It is only useful for legacy codebases.
It cannot be tested in isolation.
It is deprecated in modern browsers.

questions.explanation: "General interview questions" groups related concepts, APIs, and best practices you should be able to reason about and apply.

questions.question: When working inside "04-general-interview-questions", the most effective way to retain the material is to:

options.text: Read the core principles, implement sample code, and test understanding via quizzes.

questions.explanation: Active recall combined with hands-on practice leads to mastery.
